name: asks-kick-off-plan-or-bundle
text:
ions` (requirements.toml)** — even closer to the Overdeck model. It's an admin-owned developer message kept deliberately separate from client instructions, capped at 10k tokens, and it emits explicit "these managed instructions replace / no longer apply" notices when the policy changes mid-conversation (`codex-rs/core/src/context/world_state/managed_developer_instructions.rs`). This is designed for precisely the managed-orchestrator case.
- **`model_instructions_file`** — a trap for us: it *replaces* Codex's built-in instructions rather than adding to them. Not appropriate.
- **`AGENTS.override.md` in `$CODEX_HOME`** — overrides the global AGENTS.md for that home only; still file-based but at least scoped to the managed home rather than the user's.
- AGENTS.md discovery itself (per the [AGENTS.md guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md)) is global → repo-root → cwd, rebuilt every run, capped at 32 KiB.

**Recommendation:** replace `initCodexHome()`'s AGENTS.md copy with `developer_instructions` (or `managed_config.developer_instructions` if Overdeck wants the admin-owned, replacement-notice semantics), passed per-session. That kills the 175-stale-Codex-homes problem structurally — nothing is persisted, every launch and resume recomputes from canonical sources.

## 2. The "Overdeck-owned launch home" — explained, and what the draft did

The concept, from the uncommitted draft (tag `handoff/20260909/main`, `src/lib/claude-launch-home.ts`): today Overdeck provisions its hooks, statusline, settings, and plugins by *writing into your real `~/.claude`* — your personal harness config. The launch home inverts that. For each managed session, Overdeck builds a private Claude config directory it fully owns and points the session at it via `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Your native `~/.claude` becomes **read-only input** — the draft copies your `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, and `plugins/` into the launch home as a base layer, then overlays Overdeck's managed copies on top. Nothing ever writes back.

The clever parts of the draft:

- **Settings are merged, not overwritten** — user settings plus managed settings, with hook tables merged by event, historical Overdeck hook registrations recognized by path and de-duplicated, retired hooks (the old ask-user-question hooks) filtered out, and provider env keys (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, Bedrock/Vertex flags, …) stripped from the merged env so credentials can't leak into the overlay.
- **History and identity are persistent but private** — the launch home's `projects/` directory and `.claude.json` are symlinks into a persistent Overdeck-owned home, so transcripts survive across launches while Claude's trust acknowledgements are seeded privately instead of being clicked through in your real config.
- **Credentials get a single private refresh chain** — your `.credentials.json` is imported once into one shared Overdeck-private store; every agent's launch home symlinks to that, never to vendor-native state, so token refreshes don't race across dozens of agents.

So "launch home" = a per-session, Overdeck-owned harness profile assembled fresh at launch from (user's native state, read-only) + (Overdeck's canonical managed state) + (project skills). Status: the draft is complete-looking code but **never reviewed** — PAN-3829 is open and tracks doing it properly; the same treatment for Codex auth (Overdeck-owned auth copy instead of `~/.codex`) was in the draft too.

## 3. Skills scoping issues vs. your bundles master plan

[PAN-1655](https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/issues/1655) is narrower than what you're describing. It adds a second scoping axis to the existing one: today's only axis is *audience* (`sync-sources/skills/` = universal, `sync-sources/dev-skills/` = dev-only); PAN-1655 adds *role* — a `roles: [review, ship]` frontmatter field so a skill syncs only into the sessions of matching pipeline roles (conversation/work/review/ship/plan/test). Motivation: review-only skills currently load ambiently into work agents' context, costing tokens and firing at wrong moments. [PAN-1656](https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/issues/1656) is the dashboard side — the Skills page becomes a full management surface (browse, edit frontmatter, scope toggles, sync status, lint drift).

Neither issue covers **named bundles you toggle per scope** (global / project / issue / conversation). Your master plan is a superset: bundle definitions as first-class objects, plus a resolution chain that looks a lot like the context-layers model — global bundles, project-layer bundles, per-issue activation, per-conversation overrides. The good news is the pieces align: PAN-1655's frontmatter scoping gives skills metadata to group by, PAN-1656's management UI is where bundle toggles would live, and the launch-home work (PAN-3829) is what makes per-scope skill activation *mechanically clean* — since skills land in the launch home at spawn time, activating a bundle per conversation is just "copy a different set into this launch's `skills/`," with zero mutation of anything shared. If you want, I'd file a new issue for the bundle system that supersedes/folds in 1655+1656 rather than stretching them.

## 4. conv/2681 → filed, specced, but no work started

That conversation (codex, 2026-09-09, "Add PR-conversation linking feature") produced [PAN-3822](https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/issues/3822): **"Link pull requests to conversations through branch detection and explicit overrides"** — a well-formed spec: automatic branch-based association with server-side refresh, right-click "Link to conversation" on PR/MR URLs in transcripts as an explicit override, resolver/writer door discipline, live PR state badges on conversation rows and headers. Status: **open, unassigned, no cross-referenced PRs, no workspace or agent, no branch.** Nothing has started — it's sitting in the backlog with an `enhancement` label. Want me to kick off `pan plan PAN-3822`, or bundle it with the skills work?
label: asks_operator

name: asks-file-the-issue
text:
One fact confirmed: archived conversations do still show up in search — the indexer (`src/lib/conversation-search/indexer.ts`) works purely off transcript files on disk and has zero awareness of the archived flag. So that part already behaves the way you'd want; what's missing is the badge and action on the result.

Your instincts are right, and I'd frame the whole thing as one root cause: **Overdeck has two planes of truth for conversations — the transcript files on disk (what the search indexer reads) and the conversations DB (what every view reads) — and nothing reconciles them.** The "Conversation not found" popup isn't a search bug, it's the DB-plane UI refusing to acknowledge something the transcript plane can see plain as day. PAN-2981 covers the zombie half of that (transcript deleted, index entry alive). Your case is the mirror half: transcript alive and rendering fine, no DB row. They deserve separate fixes.

Here's how I'd approach each of your ideas:

**1. Kill the error, show the conversation with an unmanaged badge.** When `/conv/<id>` misses the conversations table, fall back to transcript discovery (the scanner in `src/lib/conversations/scanner.ts` already discovers unmanaged sessions — PAN-3012's backup proposal planned to piggyback it) and render the conversation read-only with a badge near the name: "Outside Overdeck projects · `<path>`". No toast, no redirect confusion. The transcript rendered anyway in your screenshot, so this is mostly deleting the lie and adding the label.

**2. Materialize a DB row on open, so it lands in `__no-project__`.** This is the piece that makes your "get back without searching" work. First open of an unmanaged session creates a minimal conversations row (hash-derived name, first-message preview, ended status, no project). From then on it's first-class: it shows in the `__no-project__` list, future opens skip the fallback path, and it can be archived/unarchived like anything else. Materialize-on-open beats a bulk backfill sweep — sessions nobody ever opens never pollute the list.

**3. "Add as project" from both places.** The indexer already knows the cwd (it's encoded in the transcript dir name, `-home-eltmon-Projects-<project>`), so the CTA can be genuinely one-click: badge on the Ctrl-K row and in the conversation header, click → project-creation flow prefilled with the path. On the Workspaces question — I'd say no, project is the right container. Workspaces are git worktrees tied to issue work; `<project>` is a standalone directory with no tracker. What's really wanted is a *lightweight project*: no GitHub Issues, just a named home for conversations, memory, and search scope. That's a small generalization of what `__no-project__` is today, and it gives the folder a real identity instead of an orphan bin.

**4. Archived conversations in search.** Keep them searchable (already true), add an "Archived" badge on the result row plus an Unarchive action — `pan unarchive-conversation` and the palette command already exist, so this is surfacing, not building.

**Phasing:** I'd file this as one issue with four work items — (a) route fallback + badge, (b) materialize-on-open into `__no-project__`, (c) add-as-project CTA in both surfaces, (d) archived badge + unarchive in search results. Items a+b are the core and small; c is medium; d is nearly free. And I'd leave [PAN-2981](https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/issues/2981) scoped to true zombies (deleted transcript, live index entry — prune on `unlink`), since that's a different mechanism. Worth a line in the new issue linking [PAN-3012](https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/issues/3012) too: unmanaged discovered sessions are exactly the population its backup scope control ("all discovered sessions") was designed for, so the two features share the scanner as their discovery source.

Want me to file the issue?

name: blocked-review-no-op-on-approved-pr
text:
A reviewer is live and working on the current head. Standing by.

**There was nothing to fix — the red was CI infrastructure, not lint.** The `lint` check is only an aggregator; its entire job body is `echo "lint-group: failure"; test "failure" = success`, so it went red purely because the effect group did. That group died at `curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 500`, exit code 22, during dependency setup right after `bun install` — before any lint code executed. No diagnostic output existed because no diagnostic ran.

I verified rather than taking my own word for it: `npm run lint` exits 0 with *"Effect diagnostics guard passed (231 known findings; none new)"* and *"Effect façade ratchet passed (A 1, B 4, C 28; none new)"*, and `npm run typecheck` exits 0. I also confirmed my diff against main touches no effect, ratchet, or baseline file at all — so your instruction not to raise a baseline was moot here; there was never an increase to launder.

The fix was re-running the flaked jobs (`gh run rerun 36397740176 --failed`). All 15 checks on `8f216a8b` are now green (1 skipped) and PR #4271 is back to `clean`. I left the head alone rather than merging main's 3 new commits — `merge-tree` shows no conflict, so another head would have bought nothing but another review cycle.

**One correction, because it changes the remedy:** I did signal `pan done` after the 08:30 push. It returned *"Tests re-queued for PAN-1641 (PR already approved)"* and started no review. `pan done` reads review state at the issue level while GitHub pins approvals per commit, so the approval on `f144afd6` suppressed any review of `8f216a8b`. This round I ran `pan done` **and** an explicit `pan review request` — and that was *also* refused with "PR already approved". Neither command can dispatch a review while that stale issue-level pass stands.

What finally worked was `pan review restart`, which resumed the reviewer session; `claude --model claude-opus-5-5 --name agent-pan-1641-review` is running now against this head. Worth noting as a real pipeline gap: after a conflict-resolution merge, the only verb that actually re-reviews is `restart` — `done` and `review request` both silently no-op on an approved PR, which is how a new head can sit unreviewed while looking finished.

text:
**Verdict posted: PASSED** for `async-omp-provisioning` on [PAN-1641](https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/issues/1641).

I reviewed the full item range `e990363582..75b0a6a112` as you directed — reviewing `75b0a6a112` alone would have been meaningless, since that commit only collapses two multi-line blocks to single lines to restore the launcher file-size ratchets.

**What held up.** AC1 is clean: [`src/lib/ohmypi-models.ts:17`](<path>) imports only from `node:fs/promises`, no sync fs survives anywhere in the file, and the function returns `Promise<void>`. The generator no longer imports or calls provisioning at all. The serialization at lines 109–141 is genuinely correct rather than merely plausible — map registration is synchronous through the `set`, so no two calls can both read an empty slot; `previous.catch(() => undefined)` keeps a corrupt-JSON rejection from poisoning every later call on that path; and all six live callers await the returned promise. Typecheck is clean and the three named test files pass, 92 tests.

**The one mismatch, and why it doesn't block.** AC2 claims all 9 former call sites await provisioning. Eight do. The ninth — [`src/lib/runtimes/pi.ts:371`](<path>) — passes `harness: 'ohmypi'` with a model and provisions nothing. It's the unregistered legacy Pi adapter from PAN-1989: `runtimes/index.ts:141` registers only `createOhmypiRuntimeSync`, `index.ts:104-106` normalizes both `'ohmypi'` and `'pi'` onto that adapter, and `PiRuntimeSync` is constructed nowhere outside `src/lib/runtimes/__tests__/`. That path was dead before the hoist too, so the old in-generator provisioning never fired there either — reachable behavior is identical across the change. Failing the bead would force either awaiting inside dead code or deleting it, and the surgical-changes rule forbids the deletion. I wrote the exception into the verdict notes rather than letting it pass silently.

One non-blocking gap for later: FR-3's "different paths proceed in parallel" half has no test. No acceptance criterion asks for one, so it didn't factor into the verdict.

Staying resident for the next commit delivery.
